question: Will enough non-latest-version queries exist (or be constructible) in a legal corpus to give the recency-decoupled comparison adequate statistical power?
description: The recency-decoupled design depends on obtaining enough queries whose authoritative clause version is not the latest, with enough amendment chains deep enough that multiple versions are plausibly retrieved. SituatedQA reports only ~16.5% of NQ-Open questions are context-dependent, suggesting such queries are a minority in natural corpora; if the legal analogue is similarly sparse, the non-latest stratum may be too small for reliable comparisons unless it is deliberately oversampled or synthesized from amendment history.
confidence_basis: A verified prevalence estimate and a verified alternative-context construction precedent establish that the stratum is constructed rather than sampled, so the power question reduces to corpus size and clustering; the actual counts per corpus remain unverified.
rationale: SituatedQA quantifies context-dependent questions as a modest fraction of a natural QA corpus, and deep amendment chains with distinctive validity windows are needed for the treatment to have anything to correct.
resolution: Partially resolved: the stratum is constructible by design, so power is a corpus property rather than a prevalence problem. Precedent shows context-dependent questions are a minority naturally (roughly 16.5% of NQ-Open; up to 30% by annotator judgement for answers that change over time) but that one question can be multiplied into several (context, answer) instances - verified in SituatedQA, which crowdsources alternative contexts and their answers and builds a triple per validated pair. Applied here, each multi-version clause can yield multiple target dates inside historical validity windows. The binding constraints are therefore (i) the number of clauses with two or more versions and documented per-version validity dates, (ii) query-authoring cost, and (iii) clustering of queries within clauses, which requires a clustered power calculation rather than a per-query one. Reported rates must be given weighted by natural prevalence as well as oversampled. Plan E006 measures the counts directly and returns a pre-registered go/no-go decision.
